topic.title: Why is there so much grimmsnarl

messages.content: Grimmsnarl is favored into Alakazam and has good lines into beating Crustle, both of which made up the majority of the top of the leaderboard for a while (based on the kaggle replay data, and the images here: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/pokemon-tcg-ai-battle/discussion/729926).

replies.content:
If you're playing on PTCG Live, they are in a different format with many different cards and decks. But in both the current format and the Kaggle competition format, I agree that the Grimmsnarl deck is not so strong. In particular, Dragapult Crushing Hammers is a powerful deck into Grimmsnarl. But in the Kaggle meta, there are very few good Hammer pult agents, so Grimm can run freely into these lists.

I'm still trying to figure out how to get my ML loop to work successfully :P I think I have some good ideas for decks that can run better if you ever want to chat more on it. I recommend a Hammer Pult deck with Unfair Stamp, in general, if your agent is capable of running such a list.

replies.content: The competition and skill can vary a lot between online and in person. The hammer deck has to have exponentially more complexity with how a heads or tails on a Crushing Hammer coin flip can change your strategy within each turn, so I imagine that is part of why many players are not submitting Dragapult. Along with the strategy needed by Pult to win into some of the single prize decks (using Jet Headbutt to buy a turn before using Boss's Orders to take a multi-turn KO, for example).

replies.content: If I compute e.g. Nash equilibrium deck choices with human stats, some Dragapult variant is usually the top pick, but if I use Kaggle AI agents stats, the picture is quite different. So optimising for human play might lead to different choices than optimising for agent play. However, your post made me re-run the numbers and Dragapult agents have become a lot better (now slightly favored vs Grimmsnarl, while they were losers before), so it is definitely learnable and the meta is shifting when new, stronger agents come into play.
